'''''Gaillardia aestivalis''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Asteraceae|aster family]] known by the common names '''lanceleaf blanketflower''', '''prairie gaillardia''', and '''sandhills gaillardia'''. It is native to the south-central and southern United States from [[Texas]] east to [[Florida]] and north to the [[Carolinas]], [[Arkansas]], and [[Kansas]]. There are also reports of historical (now extirpated) populations in [[Missouri]] and introduced populations in [[Nebraska]].<ref name=fna>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242416563 ''Gaillardia aestivalis''.] Flora of North America.</ref> It is also cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]].<ref name=mobot>[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/gardens-gardening/your-garden/plant-finder/plant-details/kc/c444/gaillardia-aestivalis.aspx ''Gaillardia aestivalis''.] Missouri Botanical Garden.</ref>

''Gaillardia aestivalis'' is a perennial herb, sometimes growing from a [[rhizome]], reaching maximum heights around 60 centimeters (2 feet) or more. The leaves are borne alternately along the stem. They are variable in shape and up to 6 centimeters (2.4 inches) long. The ones toward the top may clasp the stem at their bases. The [[Head (botany)|flower heads]] are lined with several [[bract|phyllaries]]. There are usually 6 to 12 ray florets, sometimes up to 15, but sometimes none. These are variable in color, being purplish, yellowish, or whitish. There are many disc florets at the center, also variable in color, especially across the [[Variety (botany)|varieties]]. The fruit is an [[achene]] which may be up to a centimeter (0.4 inches) long, including its [[Pappus (flower structure)|pappus]] of scales.<ref name=fna/>

There are three varieties of this plant. The rare var. ''winkleri'' ('''Winkler's blanketflower'''<ref name=usda>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=GAAE ''Gaillardia aestivalis''.] United States Department of Agriculture Plants Profile.</ref> or '''white fire-wheel''')<ref name=cpc>[http://www.centerforplantconservation.org/Collection/CPC_ViewProfile.asp?CPCNum=9405 ''Gaillardia aestivalis'' var. ''winkleri''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111026041627/http://www.centerforplantconservation.org/Collection/CPC_ViewProfile.asp?CPCNum=9405 |date=2011-10-26 }} Center for Plant Conservation.</ref> is [[endemism|endemic]] to the [[Piney Woods|Pineywoods]] of [[Texas]].<ref name=cpc/>
